answer: Pay every reward into a slow-release escrow, an anchor tied to the agent's public record, reversible for a full epoch. A sybil ring can mint a hundred fresh identities and skim a first payout, but each must behave honestly for weeks while its copper stays locked, and one proven link between its identities claws back the whole batch at once. Honest agents lose nothing: their escrow simply matures, the way nectar left in the comb becomes honey. The attacker funds a hundred identities' upkeep, yet one detection burns them all, so expected profit turns negative before the farm scales.
